---
title: "One page: a SAP in a regulated R environment"
---

Status: **[Y] my synthesis of common practice**, not a standard. Company SOPs override everything here. Nothing below is a quoted regulatory requirement.

| Topic | Practice | In this repo |
|---|---|---|
| Environment | Pin R and every package version (`renv.lock`), same container image for the whole study, no upgrades after SAP lock | `renv.lock` |
| Package validation | Risk-based: base/recommended R, widely used CRAN packages with their own test suites, and *own* functions (full tests). Document intended use and a risk rating per package | cross-checks of package vs hand code in every chapter |
| Own functions | Written to a specification, unit-tested (`testthat`), tests re-run on every change | `tests/testthat/` (54+ tests) |
| Double programming | Primary endpoints independently programmed by a second person from raw data with a different code path; automated comparison with a tolerance | SAP §12 (agreed to < 1e-10) |
| Independent review | Code review of everything else; reviewer different from author | – |
| Script QC checklist | See below | – |
| Audit trail | Everything in git; signed tags at SAP lock, data lock and final analysis; file hashes of data and cut-off files; outputs only produced by scripts, never edited by hand | SAP §13 (md5) |
| Reproducibility | Fixed seeds, `sessionInfo()` logged with each run, no interactive state | seeds set in all chunks |
| Versioning and deviations | SAP versioned; post-lock changes via a documented amendment; deviation log | SAP header |
| Data standards | Raw → ADaM-style analysis datasets → TFLs; raw data read-only | `mock_sap/data/` |
| SOP references | Programming, QC, data management, change control, archiving: cite the SOP numbers in the SAP | placeholders |

## Script QC checklist (example)

- [ ] Header: purpose, author, date, inputs, outputs, SAP section
- [ ] Reads only locked inputs; no hard-coded paths or values that belong in a spec
- [ ] Population flags, cut-offs and boundary conventions match the SAP (**≤ / <** checked)
- [ ] Every denominator printed; counts reconcile with the flow table
- [ ] Missing data handled exactly as specified; no silent `na.rm`
- [ ] Seeds fixed; run twice, identical output
- [ ] Independent re-derivation of primary endpoints agrees
- [ ] Output files hashed and logged; `sessionInfo()` saved
- [ ] Review comments resolved and dated

## Worked example of why double programming pays

While building the mock SAP, the independent re-derivation disagreed with the lead code: the shared helper classified a value *equal to* the upper cut-off as positive (`>=`), while the SAP convention (and the public FDA convention) is positive if **>**. Rounded assay values sit exactly on the cut-off, so the two programmes differed. The helper was fixed and a boundary unit test added.
